messages.content: You are an experienced sales director. Estimate the probability (between 0 and 1) that this contract will be SIGNED, as opposed to lost or delayed for a long time. Veto holders must all agree for the contract to be signed. Be calibrated.

Deal: Port-Lazen – Kerlis submarine cable · seller: Ondine Subsea · buyer: Nordlink Bay Consortium
Key actors (id | name | role | organization | veto | influence):
- claire_dantec | Claire Dantec | Chair of the consortium | Nordlink Bay Consortium | - | 0.95
- julien_marec | Julien Marec | Chief Technology Officer | Baltis Telecom | - | 0.60
- marion_kervella | Marion Kervella | Marine Permits Officer | Kerlis Coastal Agency | VETO | 0.40
- paul_ternaud | Paul Ternaud | ADB legal | Atlantic Development Bank | - | 0.40
- sophie_lenoir | Sophie Lenoir | Chief Financial Officer | Baltis Telecom | VETO | 0.80
- thomas_riou | Thomas Riou | Relationship Manager | Atlantic Development Bank | VETO | 0.90
- yann_le_goff | Yann Le Goff | Head of Procurement | Kerlis Connect | - | 0.50

Debriefs dictated by the sales rep, oldest first:

[2026-09-15]
Debrief of the kick-off meeting on September 15, Port-Lazen – Kerlis project.

So, first real meeting with everyone around the table. Claire Dantec, the chair of the Nordlink Bay consortium, opened the meeting. She mostly talked about the schedule: she wants the cable in service before the end of 2028, that's her absolute priority. She didn't take a position on suppliers, she stayed very neutral.

Thomas Riou, from the Atlantic Development Bank, was there. He said the bank was "interested in principle" but that a full environmental impact study would be needed before any commitment. He asked us for a note on our experience laying cable in protected areas.

Julien Marec, the CTO of Baltis, asked a lot of questions about the repeaters, he seemed happy with the answers.

Oceanix Cables has also been consulted, Claire said so openly.

Next steps: send the note on protected areas to Thomas Riou by the end of September, and prepare the technical review in early October.


[2026-10-06]
Debrief of the technical review on October 6, with Baltis Telecom and Kerlis Connect.

Very good meeting on the technical side. Julien Marec approved our repeater architecture, he even said he would defend it internally. Yann Le Goff, the head of procurement at Kerlis Connect, was there too. He is harder to read: he mostly talked about late-delivery penalties and guarantees, he wants stronger penalties than what we offer. I don't know if he leans towards us or towards Oceanix.

He mentioned that the award decision will go through a committee where Claire Dantec has the final say, but that the bank must have given its agreement in principle before that.

Nobody has any news of the impact study, I think it hasn't even been launched yet.

Next steps: send a revised proposal on penalties to Yann Le Goff, and chase Thomas Riou about the protected areas note, he hasn't replied.


[2026-10-22]
Participants
- Thomas Riou (rel. manager)
- Paul Ternaud (ADB legal)
- note author ("me")

Key points
- Environmental impact study: final version expected BEFORE credit committee.
- Credit committee: mid-December ?? (to be confirmed).
- Bank guarantee on the payment plan: he finds the idea interesting, to be investigated further.

Positions expressed
- T. Riou: "no financing until the study is approved"
- P. Ternaud wants to review penalty clauses.

Actions and deadlines
- Send study summary to T. Riou before 15/11!
- Dig into the bank guarantee on the payment plan idea.

[2026-10-27]
Debrief of Tuesday's meeting with the Nordlink Bay consortium, Port-Lazen – Kerlis cable project.

Well, a rather positive meeting overall. Julien Marec, the CTO of Baltis Telecom, is clearly on our side: he said our repeater solution was "the most robust technically". On the other hand their CFO, Sophie Lenoir, insisted a lot on the payment schedule, she wants to spread it over four years instead of three, otherwise she won't sign off.

On financing, the Atlantic Development Bank is still waiting for the environmental impact study before committing. Thomas Riou, their relationship manager, wasn't there, we haven't seen him for six weeks now. I think we need to chase him.

The competitor, Oceanix Cables, was mentioned twice, apparently they offered a lower price, but I'm not sure of the amount, maybe ten percent less.

Next steps: send a four-year payment schedule proposal before the 15th, and set up a meeting with the bank before the end of the month.


Lessons from the rep's past deals (other contracts, validated by the rep; use them only where they fit):
- [signed] When a finance veto holder blocks over upfront concentration, reframe the price as milestone payments tied to acceptance records so their own cash curve validates compliance. (relevant when: a finance veto holder ties approval to a cash ceiling and flags a large deposit as non-compliant)
- [signed] Align the lender's tranche releases with the customer's acceptance milestones early, so the bank is observed to follow once the finance holder's curve turns positive. (relevant when: a private infrastructure lender makes support conditional on smoothing disbursements)
- [signed] Keep technical and operations supporters engaged while reworking commercials, so a higher face price is observed to remain defensible on technical and whole-life value. (relevant when: a technical champion supports capacity while finance threatens to switch to a cheaper rival)
- [lost] When a lending veto holder ties approval to an independent audit, treat the auditor and the study timetable as the commercial critical path and maintain direct engagement with the lender. (relevant when: a lending veto holder says financing approval must wait for an external environmental study)
- [lost] When an independent certifier will not pre-validate an incomplete file, do not plan to catch up in parallel; re-baseline schedule, cost and risk with the finance veto holder immediately. (relevant when: an independent auditor refuses any interim validation and requires a complete file)
- [lost] When signature depends on lender attestation and partners reject waiting costs, secure a funded waiting agreement early rather than observing the financing line drift until it is reallocated. (relevant when: a finance veto holder blocks signature pending lender attestation while a co-funding partner refuses standby costs)
- [signed] Observed that a finance veto holder who ties approval to upfront cost can be moved by reframing to capped multi-year total cost plus contractual price and performance caps. (relevant when: a finance veto holder frames the decision as CAPEX too high versus a cheaper legacy alternative)
- [signed] Observed to secure a cautious lender by offering penalized efficiency guarantees, delay and performance penalties, and a bank guarantee early rather than treating financing as a final formality. (relevant when: a private financing risk holder conditions support on enforceable performance protection)
- [signed] Observed to convert prudence into support by staging a live pilot with measured performance in front of stakeholders and obtaining public validation from the consulting engineer. (relevant when: a technical champion supports a novel architecture but a consulting engineer and a chief executive remain prudent)
- [lost] When a procurement veto holder ties support to schedule security, observed lesson is to lock agreed total-cost and risk criteria with them before a low-price indicative offer resets the negotiation to price alone. (relevant when: The procurement veto holder initially favours quality to protect schedule but then asks to match a cheaper rival.)
- [lost] When a finance veto holder and an external lender focus on CAPEX and financability, observed lesson is to engage them early on cost transparency and funding constraints rather than relying on the technical chooser alone. (relevant when: A finance veto holder demands a full cost breakdown and frames the decision around financability.)
- [lost] When an independent certifier can level the technical field, observed lesson is to build a commercial and lifecycle-cost defence in parallel and not let the technical argument carry the deal alone. (relevant when: An independent technical certifier is expected to differentiate the offers but rates both options as acceptable.)
- [delayed] Engage the certification veto holder and the finance veto holder early, even when the project owner and technical lead are enthusiastic, because late certification requirements were observed to freeze financing. (relevant when: A certification veto holder is absent from early technical alignment and financing is not discussed in detail.)
- [delayed] Treat certification approval as a predecessor to bankability in the sales plan when a lender conditions closing on it, and sequence testing, audits, and documentation accordingly. (relevant when: A finance veto holder explicitly ties financial closing to prior certification approval.)
- [delayed] Secure explicit schedule contingency with installation partners when certification timelines are uncertain, as resource reallocation was observed alongside extended approval delays. (relevant when: An installation contractor signals that a key vessel or crew may be reallocated if the schedule slips.)
- [signed] When a deployment veto holder blocks on operational risk, arrange a live reference visit with field measurements rather than adding slides; observed shift followed direct inspection. (relevant when: A high-influence technical veto holder attacks schedule and network-break risk and cites past failures by others.)
- [signed] When a finance veto holder conditions funding on guarantees, offer phased milestones each gated by independent audit; observed alignment followed that structure. (relevant when: A financing veto holder withholds approval pending firm schedule guarantees and third-party quality control.)
- [signed] When an independent certifier demands field evidence, have metrics validated publicly on site in front of stakeholders; observed credibility followed public validation. (relevant when: An independent certifier stays cautious and asks for additional field data while the technical champion already supports the architecture.)
- [lost] When a finance veto holder ties approval to the budget cycle, treat a missing CAPEX line as a blocking issue and pause technical work until an OPEX or interim funding path is validated. (relevant when: A finance veto holder says no CAPEX line can be booked until a future budget cycle)
- [lost] When bank funding depends on a voted budget, sequence the budget vote before detailed sizing and make the lender requirement visible to the economic buyer early. (relevant when: An infrastructure lender says a voted budget resolution is required to price and take the file to credit committee)
- [lost] When the top executive avoids overruling finance ahead of a board vote, observed enthusiasm does not substitute for arbitration, so secure an explicit pre-board decision or a reduced scope that finance will present. (relevant when: A chief executive stays enthusiastic but defers to finance and does not arbitrate before the board)
- [signed] When a legal veto holder ties approval to completing a risk analysis, observed progress stays technical-only until caps and insurance language are tabled early in redrafts. (relevant when: a legal veto holder says she will not comment until her risk and cap analysis is finished)
- [signed] When a legal reviewer blocks on liability and penalties, observed movement follows a concrete counter-proposal such as a dual cap and shared deductible rather than general reassurance. (relevant when: a legal veto holder raises a long list of blocking points on liability, insurance and delay penalties)
- [signed] When an independent auditor controls technical credibility, observed support consolidates after a live operational demonstration validated as compliant with his framework. (relevant when: an independent technical auditor must validate methods against his own framework)
- [delayed] When a finance veto holder ties approval to a usage-based cost split, observed risk is deadlock unless the allocation model is renegotiated before further technical work. (relevant when: a finance veto holder openly rejects the proposed split of an unexpected cost increase)
- [delayed] When two veto holders defend opposing cost keys, observed pattern is delay until a jointly accepted formula is secured rather than parallel technical validation. (relevant when: a technical veto holder makes signature conditional on rebalancing costs while the finance veto holder refuses)
- [delayed] When a lender makes funding conditional on partner alignment, observed need is to treat partner agreement as the critical path and sequence selling effort accordingly. (relevant when: a project lender states that financing cannot proceed without prior agreement between partners)
- [lost] A board chair who controls scoring weights and favors local servicing must be engaged before criteria lock; once the weighting is validated, observed technical superiority no longer compensates. (relevant when: When a board-level veto holder starts assigning a large share of the score to local presence and local stock.)
- [lost] A finance veto holder who ties approval to locally collateralized guarantees needs an alternative security structure early; observed persistence of the demand blocks progress if left unaddressed. (relevant when: When a financing veto holder makes approval conditional on guarantees backed by in-territory assets and local surety.)
- [lost] A private certifier who can impose extended testing that conflicts with the installation window must be de-risked in parallel with technical selling; observed delay creates a schedule disqualification even when testing looks workable. (relevant when: When a private certifier conditions approval on several months of additional testing while installation faces a seasonal weather deadline.)
- [signed] When a procurement veto holder pressures on price alongside a finance veto holder worried about CAPEX, observed support from the technical evaluator alone does not hold the short-list; trade any investment reduction for a longer locked-price maintenance term that moves spend to smoothed OPEX. (relevant when: a procurement veto holder frames the bid as overpriced versus a named competitor and a finance veto holder calls CAPEX too heavy)
- [signed] When a finance veto holder prefers smoothed OPEX and a lender observes the financing, offer an extended maintenance with locked annuities and availability penalties to turn finance and the lender into supporters rather than conceding price alone. (relevant when: a finance veto holder and a lender need multi-year visibility before they will support the deal)
- [signed] When a co-user with veto power stays neutral on price but worries about cohabitation, explicitly guarantee priority access slots during maintenance to keep that veto neutral-to-positive while the commercial negotiation closes. (relevant when: a co-user with veto power stays neutral and asks for priority access during maintenance windows)
- [lost] Map succession risk early and build a parallel relationship with a likely technical successor from a competing background, rather than relying on one champion. (relevant when: When a deal relies on a single technical champion and rumors emerge that the champion may leave)
- [lost] Treat the installation subcontractor as a de facto influencer and lock in its method, tooling and cost commitment before a specification can be reopened. (relevant when: When an installation subcontractor initially favors a lighter solution but later seeks to secure its campaign with familiar technology)
- [lost] Quantify requalification, interface and certification cost with the finance veto holder early, so a price discount is not observed as insufficient against later risk costs. (relevant when: When a finance veto holder and a lender make unconditional certification a condition for funding)
- [signed] When a lender makes funding conditional on an independent audit, treat the audit as the critical path and align scope, access, and timing early with the auditor. (relevant when: a lender with veto power ties funding release to independent technical validation)
- [signed] When a finance guardian waits for external validation, sequence the close by securing the technical sign-off first, then observed budget approval follows. (relevant when: a finance veto holder defers their budget decision until an external party rules)
- [signed] When a deal faces a waiting period for validation, keep an active technical champion defending performance in front of the sponsor to sustain support. (relevant when: a long validation pause creates risk of losing momentum with the sponsor)
- [lost] When a finance veto holder ties approval to the budget cycle and cash preservation, secure joint success criteria and a conditional path to approval before re-costing, as observed when repeated rework did not advance the decision. (relevant when: a finance veto holder ties approval to cash position and asks for full budget and financing structure early)
- [lost] When a bank financing contact conditions support on equity preservation, align the commercial phasing directly with that financing condition and test it early, as observed when prudence hardened into withdrawal. (relevant when: a lending veto holder makes bridge funding conditional on preserving equity)
- [lost] When a final decision-maker avoids arbitration and proposes delay, escalate to force an explicit go, no-go, or conditions for yes, as observed when consensus-seeking left the project exposed to a freeze. (relevant when: a final decision-maker defers choice to a later investment committee while budget pressure grows)
- [delayed] Treat a grid connection veto holder as the critical path from discovery and get a written lead-time range in weeks, as observed when the study plus works signal preceded a long delay. (relevant when: a grid connection manager first mentions a capacity study plus new high-voltage works on a deal needing extra megawatts)
- [delayed] Sequence a finance veto holder who requires written proof of power availability before any equipment commitment, as observed when funding stayed blocked without that attestation. (relevant when: a project finance veto holder ties fund release to a firm written date for power availability)
- [delayed] Align early with an operations veto holder who refuses installation without guaranteed supply to define phasing and go/no-go criteria, as observed when installation waited on the grid schedule. (relevant when: an operations director veto holder states zero tolerance for customer interruption during retrofit works)
- [signed] When a veto holder ties cost share to traffic doubts, reframe the offer around risk-sharing with a guaranteed revenue floor rather than re-arguing forecasts. (relevant when: when a veto-holding partner disputes cost-sharing and doubts traffic forecasts)
- [signed] Sequence a bankable deal by first securing the reluctant operator, observed to unlock the lender, rather than pressing the lender for approval in parallel. (relevant when: when a lender makes funding conditional on long-term joint commitment)
- [signed] Keep the technical champion visible in financial forums to sustain momentum when commercial veto holders stall. (relevant when: when a technical champion is enthusiastic but absent from financial decisions)
- [lost] A lead lender risk veto holder who ties approval to the budget cycle and loan drawdown needs early direct engagement on guarantees, observed before the technical solution is locked. (relevant when: When a lead lender veto holder starts talking about a standard guarantee grid before financial review)
- [lost] A certification veto holder who can suspend qualification if coverage is incomplete needs a parallel compliance track, observed to align with the lender rather than the technical champion late in the deal. (relevant when: When a certifier veto holder asks for proof on winter performance and traceability without endorsing the approach)
- [lost] A cooperative shareholder veto holder who fears capital calls needs reassurance on financial security separate from technical preference, observed to follow the lender once guarantees become the issue. (relevant when: When a cooperative co-shareholder veto holder expresses worry about risk to its members and avoids taking a position)
- [signed] When a legal veto holder flags standard liability caps as insufficient early, observed to engage them in clause-by-clause workshops to reshape the cap structure before the formal offer review. (relevant when: A legal veto holder signals early that standard caps are insufficient for long outages.)
- [signed] When a finance veto holder ties approval to a fixed budget cycle envelope, observed to keep any liability compromise inside that envelope so financial approval is not reopened. (relevant when: A finance veto holder insists on a single global envelope validated by a funder.)
- [signed] When a lender follows the legal veto holder on residual risk, observed to offer funder-readable proof such as supplemental insurance taken by the seller to allow alignment without changing the price envelope. (relevant when: A private lender defers to legal on residual risk and waits for final proof of cover.)
- [delayed] Treat a certification holder who ties approval to evolving standards as a critical path risk and co-build a qualification plan early, rather than relying on a technical champion. (relevant when: a certification authority signals an unstable standard and requests additional testing)
- [delayed] Engage the budget veto holder from kickoff with quantified option economics, because observed late cost-comparison requests reopen scope. (relevant when: a budget veto holder who was absent early starts asking for a stripped-down cost comparison)
- [delayed] When a financing veto holder conditions closing on bankability, bring revised revenue hypotheses and risk-sharing options quickly instead of repeating the same tariff. (relevant when: a project financier repeatedly refuses the pricing and asks for revised revenue assumptions)
- [lost] Engage purchasing and finance veto holders from the first site visit, as observed technical enthusiasm alone did not move price-led decision makers later. (relevant when: When a technical sponsor and an operations user are enthusiastic but finance and purchasing veto holders are absent from early visits)
- [lost] Reframe a technically superior offer into finance-approved TCO and budget terms early when a price-only rule is signaled, as observed continued technical optimism did not prevent a 60% price weight. (relevant when: When word circulates that purchasing wants a strict price-led tender while the team feels technically ahead)
- [lost] Build a joint case with the lender and the construction partner on total risk and lifecycle cost, as observed late alignment of those influencers with the low-price option left the discount insufficient. (relevant when: When a project finance bank states a preference for low CAPEX and the construction partner favors simpler installation)

content: {"probability": 0.18, "rationale": "Three vetoes block: Thomas Riou (0.9) - no financing until environmental study approved, study not launched Oct 6 with mid-Dec credit committee impossible and no contact for 6 weeks; Sophie Lenoir (0.8) - refuses 3-yr schedule, wants 4-yr, plus 10% cheaper Oceanix pressure; Marion Kervella permits veto (0.4) never engaged. Fits lost lesson: lender ties approval to independent audit = treat study timetable as critical path with direct lender engagement - not done; and delayed lesson on certification as predecessor to bankability."}
